source_snapshot.procedure: Stress GPU, establish maximum Watts, set all fans low, verify high temperature with reduced frequency/power and PROCHOT SEL, then power off, restore fans and power on.
source_snapshot.criteria: Maximum GPU frequency before trigger; lower frequency/power during throttle; correct SEL; clean power-off and recovery.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 50 attended and 50 machine minutes; setup requests clearing logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; queries temperature, GPU-idle reason and clocks over unsafe SSH, leaving physical heat to an operator.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; exact UUID/PCI/MIG scope, fixed workload, GPU thermal reason mapping, power/frequency phase evidence, bounded fan control, max-fan interlock and recovery.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes operator thermal involvement but queries only GPU-idle plus clocks, omitting power, exact device identity, BMC SEL, fan safety and post-power recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly distinguishes thermal/PROCHOT throttling from idle, power-cap and software-clock reasons and keeps both source baseline metrics: expected power and performance clock.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Multi-GPU servers require stable UUID/PCI identity through telemetry, BMC event mapping and reboot recovery. A throttle flag from one GPU or MIG context cannot validate another device, and lower clocks are meaningful only when the same device remains highly utilized under the fixed workload.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate GPU thermal/PROCHOT throttling under a fixed load, including reduced clocks and power, correct BMC SEL, safe fan-controller restoration and normal GPU recovery after controlled power-off/on.
original_method: Bind the case to exact GPU UUID/PCI/MIG scope, establish normal-cooling performance-clock and power baselines under a fixed workload, apply only approved bounded fan reduction, correlate utilization, temperature, clocks, power, thermal throttle reasons, fan RPM and BMC SEL, then restore cooling and verify post-power-on device identity and health.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor defines GPU-specific thermal and fan controls; an operator supervises external instruments and emergency cooling, restores the controller and validates physical recovery around power-off/on.
required_inputs: Power cap and expected normal-cooling power/clock range
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated target with no active jobs
Keep workload constant for phase comparison
Stop on wrong device, fan/sensor loss, unsafe temperature or ambiguous throttle reason
Do not automatically repeat an unsafe stage
agent_execution_scope: Run fixed load under normal cooling
Collect synchronized utilization, temperature, clocks, power and throttle reasons
Restore cooling and support controlled power cycle
engineer_actions: Approve device scope, load and limits
Approve fan controls and emergency path
Resolve maximum-Watts/clock expectations and throttle reason

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `nvidia-smi` is relevant telemetry, but querying only `gpu_idle` and clocks cannot prove thermal PROCHOT; the unsafe SSH omits UUID/PCI/MIG binding, utilization, power, fan RPM, BMC SEL and recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use supported GPU telemetry keyed by UUID/PCI to capture utilization, temperature, clocks, power, complete throttle reasons and driver/XID state throughout fixed-load normal-cooling and approved fan-reduction phases, correlated with BMC SEL.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 50/50-minute scope, source maximum-power observation, criteria maximum-frequency baseline, throttled frequency/power decrease, SEL and recovery remain; log clearing is excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a synchronized per-GPU trace with UUID/PCI/MIG, workload utilization, requested/actual clocks, power draw/cap, temperature, complete throttle mask, fan RPM and BMC event identity across baseline, trigger and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact device provenance and separates true thermal throttle from idle, cap or software-clock limiting while enforcing safe cooling control.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A GPU-idle flag and clock snapshot can falsely attribute an unloaded or capped device as thermally throttled.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor/BMC terminology may call GPU thermal signaling something other than CPU PROCHOT; the approved mapping must define the precise expected flag and SEL record.

project_override_considerations: The Project must publish the GPU-model-specific throttle mask, power/clock baseline, BMC event mapping, fan envelope and recovery. CPU PROCHOT evidence cannot be reused and GPU index alone is not stable identity.
expected_evidence: Fixed workload and normal-cooling power/clock/utilization baseline
Synchronized GPU temperature, clocks, power and complete throttle reasons
Fan command/actual RPM and external instrumentation
Exact-GPU decoded BMC SEL and XID/kernel evidence
Cooling restore, power-off/on, enumeration/health/data integrity and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure's maximum Watts and Criteria's maximum frequency are complementary baseline observations under GPU stress, followed by a shared requirement for both to decrease during thermal throttling. They expand evidence rather than define competing objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: GPU telemetry, identity mapping, workload and approved fan controls are normal project/vendor inputs. Execution blocks if true thermal reason or safe recovery cannot be established.

review_improvement: Prevents GPU-idle or power-cap behavior on the wrong device from being accepted as PROCHOT and adds full device recovery and BMC correlation.
independent_technical_reasoning: GPU clocks and power fall for many nonthermal reasons, including idle, application phase, power caps and clock locks. Under stable high utilization, only a complete vendor throttle-reason mask plus temperature transition and matching BMC event can attribute the reduction to thermal protection. UUID/PCI identity must survive power recovery to prove the same accelerator was tested.
